title: Parents' friends' attitudes; Celestin as hero and his funeral
summary: Friends all approved of jazz. She recalls Celestin's kind words when they met again and attending his funeral as a press member.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, what did your parents' fans think of it? Did they universally like it, too?

They did. They did. Some of them were not as musical as my father. And... But they all condoned it. I mean, I don't have any recollection of any of them thinking it was... fresh. You know, they all... To my recollection, thought of it highly. Of course, we did, too. And I have... All your friends? Mm-hmm. As I say, we were a very dancing crowd. We sang and danced, and... Celestine was a hero to me. I mean, I can remember seeing him. I had been away a great deal, and I saw him about 12 years ago, and he hadn't seen me because he had been away, and it wasn't like the old days when he used to play at so many of the parties where I danced. And he said, um... Well, Miss Esther, he said, I've thought of you often, but I haven't seen you around, and I remember you and your sister harmonizing together. He said, And I thought maybe you had made the big-time stuff, and it's gotten on Broadway. And I said, Well, Celestine, no, I got married and had children instead. Not that I ever would have made the big-time stuff, but I said, That thing is a wonderful compliment coming from you to think that I could have, and we shook hands. And I thought very... So I went to his funeral, and God was... Being a member of the press, we were very near his coffin. It was a beautiful ceremony, very interesting, highly religious. And of course, the long line of people are all marching with the band. It was very impressive, but I think a great, great loss to New Orleans, and one that furthered jazz a great deal.
